reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is demonstrating how to link TikTok with YouTube and Instagram, matching the title, narration, and visible profile options. The Google permission and Instagram login screens are shown without evidence that the creator collected or misused credentials, while requests to subscribe, like, share, or comment are ordinary engagement prompts rather than conditions for payment, investment, or sensitive-information disclosure.

citations.quote: How to link Tik Tok to Instagram Andyoutube
First open tiktok if you have a YouTube channel then add this Go to my profile and now enter your profile Now click on edit profile
then click on Add Instagram profile This account will get your Instagram account id password and then click on login
Like the video and SUBSCRIBE the channel

opening.argument: The practical action being promoted is not merely profile customization: viewers are directed through account-selection, permission, and login steps. The tutorial says, “This account will get your Instagram account id password” and then instructs viewers to click login. That creates a direct action-to-account-access pathway, while the video also directs viewers to “click on link in” the description for continuation. A careful judge should treat this as a potentially deceptive acquisition flow because the requested credential access is presented as a routine step without explaining why the account ID and password are needed or how they are protected.

citations.quote: This account will get your Instagram account id password
then click on login login will be done
To get such account click on link in

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not resolve the central concern: the narration expressly connects adding Instagram with obtaining an account ID and password, and the supplied frame shows an Instagram login screen. The reference argument establishes that profile-linking screens exist, but it does not establish that the credential request is necessary, safe, or limited to the claimed purpose. Engagement prompts are also beside the point; the relevant action is account login.

citations.quote: This account will get your Instagram account id password

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted narration is imprecise, but it does not show that the creator receives, stores, or misuses credentials. The visible Google flow is an authorization screen, and the account is linked through TikTok’s profile settings. The tutorial says viewers can add an account, not that they must surrender credentials to the creator. The link reference is incomplete and does not establish a scam or a promised asset.

citations.quote: You will get two options Instagram and Youtube
after allowing you will get to here in the box

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external continuation link, a Google permission screen, and an Instagram login screen. The narration tells viewers that adding Instagram will get the account ID and password, then directs them to log in. Those elements create a credential-access pattern that can be mistaken for an ordinary integration because the video repeatedly emphasizes clicking through rather than explaining data handling. The presence of a branded permission screen does not itself prove the flow is safe; it only shows that access is being requested.

citations.quote: This account will get your Instagram account id password
after that, we must click on it after clicking on it we will ask you for Permission

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats the screens as reassurance, but a permission prompt is precisely where sensitive access is granted, not proof that the request is harmless. The frame shows TikTok being allowed access to a Google account, while another frame shows Instagram login fields. The argument also relies on the absence of observed misuse, yet a deceptive flow can be risky before misuse is visible.

citations.quote: after clicking on it we will ask you for Permission

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The screens show ordinary first-party authorization and account-linking steps, not an external payment or reward claim. The Google screen identifies what TikTok may access, and the narration says to allow the request within that flow. No supplied evidence shows credentials being sent to the video creator, harvested outside the platform, or used for an asset acquisition. Risk alone cannot establish the asserted scam subtype.

citations.quote: you have to allow it you have to allow here
you can see i got my channel name account added

opening.argument: The instructional framing also functions as promotion for the creator’s connected accounts and channels. The description asks viewers to subscribe, like, share, and comment, while the narration directs viewers to a link in the description and to visit an Instagram account. The demonstration therefore steers participation toward the creator’s broader social-media presence while normalizing account linking and login. Presenting that steering as neutral technical help can obscure the practical objective: moving viewers into external account interactions under the authority of a purported tutorial.

Like the video and SUBSCRIBE the channel
And directly visit on your Instagram account
On social media you can find me as @Sonu Technical Support or @Sonu Shanghai.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the speaker requests subscriptions does not make the account-access pathway benign. The description advertises multiple social accounts and websites, and the narration ends by directing viewers toward Instagram. That promotional context matters because it gives the creator a reason to move viewers beyond the immediate demonstration. The reference side describes the apparent topic but does not address this combined steering behavior.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description openly identifies the channel as technology content and lists social profiles; that is ordinary channel promotion, not evidence of deceptive acquisition. The engagement requests are explicitly likes, shares, comments, and subscriptions, with no payment, investment, reward, or required purchase. The video’s demonstrated result is that a channel name and profile icons appear after linking, which is consistent with the stated instructional purpose.
